whys.evidence: Lane 0 B1 handoffs on the AIDLC board; lint/context-map.ts names this file as the aidlc-runner-gen LEGACY_BRIDGES reader.

exceptions.reason: The single port through which the lint layer reaches the eslint package.

whys.why: Why does lint/eslint-port.ts import the eslint package?
whys.because: The flat config modules and custom rules need ESLint's Linter and Rule types, and this file is the one place they take them from.
whys.evidence: lint/standards.ts, lint/no-comments.ts and eslint.config.ts import from lint/eslint-port.ts

whys.why: Why do the flat config modules and custom rules need ESLint's types?
whys.because: ESLint itself loads eslint.config.ts and calls each custom rule's create function, so their shapes are fixed by ESLint's plugin interface.
whys.evidence: Rule.RuleModule and Linter.Config in node_modules/eslint/lib/types/index.d.ts

whys.why: Why does ESLint's plugin interface fix those shapes rather than a type the repository owns?
whys.because: The repository chose ESLint as its lint gate when Biome was retired, and a gate's configuration is written in the host tool's own format.
whys.evidence: package.json devDependencies pin eslint 10.11.0 and no longer list @biomejs/biome

whys.why: Why was ESLint chosen as the lint gate when Biome was retired?
whys.because: The boundary rules need no-restricted-imports patterns and AST selectors per context, which ESLint's flat config expresses and Biome's configuration cannot.
whys.evidence: lint/restrictions.ts builds no-restricted-imports patterns and no-restricted-syntax selectors

whys.why: Why do the boundary rules need import patterns and AST selectors per context?
whys.because: The clean-architecture rebuild enforces the context map's dependency arrows mechanically, so every arrow becomes an import restriction checked on every file.
whys.evidence: lint/context-map.ts CONTEXT_MAP declares dependsOn for each context

whyChain.rootCause: The rebuild enforces the context map's dependency arrows mechanically through ESLint, so ESLint is a dependency the lint layer wraps at one port.
whyChain.rootCheck: Read lint/context-map.ts and lint/restrictions.ts on 2026-11-08: CONTEXT_MAP still declares dependsOn arrows and srcImportRestrictions still turns them into no-restricted-imports patterns.
whyChain.readback: The rebuild enforces the context map's arrows mechanically through ESLint, therefore the boundary rules are ESLint patterns and selectors, therefore ESLint is the lint gate, therefore the config modules and rules need ESLint's types, therefore lint/eslint-port.ts imports the eslint package as their one port.

exceptions.reason: The single port through which the lint layer reads the runtime's built-in module list.

whys.why: Why does lint/node-builtins.ts import node:module?
whys.because: The node-import-protocol rule needs the runtime's list of built-in names to tell a bare built-in such as fs from a package.
whys.evidence: lint/node-import-protocol.ts builds BARE_BUILTINS from NODE_BUILTINS

whys.why: Why does the protocol rule need to tell a bare built-in from a package?
whys.because: A bare specifier like fs can be shadowed by an installed package of that name, while node:fs always resolves to the runtime, so the rule reports the unprefixed form.
whys.evidence: https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#node-imports

whys.why: Why does the repository report the unprefixed form instead of allowing it?
whys.because: Biome's useNodejsImportProtocol enforced the prefix before ESLint replaced Biome, and the gate keeps a successor for every rule Biome enforced.
whys.evidence: lint/standards.ts registers aidlc/node-import-protocol beside lint/biome-successor.ts

whys.why: Why does the gate keep a successor for every rule Biome enforced?
whys.because: Retiring a rule without a successor would let debt-zone code regress silently while the ratchet still reads green.
whys.evidence: lint/boundary-baseline.json records counts per rule category for 1609 debt files

whys.why: Why would the ratchet read green while debt-zone code regresses?
whys.because: The baseline counts only findings of rules that run, so a rule that stops running drops its category to zero instead of failing.
whys.evidence: lint/gate/domain/violation-ratchet.ts increasesOver compares measured counts with recorded counts

whyChain.rootCause: The baseline counts only rules that run, so the protocol rule must keep running, and it needs the built-in list that node:module holds.
whyChain.rootCheck: Read lint/gate/domain/violation-ratchet.ts on 2026-11-08: increasesOver reports only measured counts above recorded ones, so a category that stops running never fails.
whyChain.readback: The baseline counts only rules that run, therefore every Biome rule keeps a successor, therefore the protocol rule tells bare built-ins from packages, therefore it needs the runtime's built-in list, therefore lint/node-builtins.ts imports node:module.

exceptions.reason: The single place the lint layer reads which harnesses exist, from the harness folders on disk.

whys.why: Why does lint/harness-folders.ts import node:fs and node:url?
whys.because: It lists the folders under harness/ and src/hosts/ when the lint config loads, and those folder names are the harness names the boundary rules refuse outside a host bundle.
whys.evidence: lint/restrictions.ts builds harnessName and harnessPath from HARNESS_FOLDER_NAMES

whys.why: Why are the harness names read from folder names rather than written in a list?
whys.because: A written list is a second copy of the harness set that drifts when a harness is added, so an eighth harness would need a lint edit to be guarded.
whys.evidence: lint/context-map.ts HARNESS_NAMES held 12 hand-written entries beside the 7 folders under harness/

whys.why: Why does a drifting copy of the harness set matter to the boundary rules?
whys.because: The rules refuse harness names in production code outside src/hosts, so a harness missing from the copy could be named anywhere without a finding.
whys.evidence: lint/boundaries.ts productionSyntax adds harnessNames to every non-fixture src layer

whys.why: Why must production code outside src/hosts never name a harness?
whys.because: Each harness difference belongs in a host bundle behind a port, so the contexts stay one implementation for every harness the method ships to.
whys.evidence: lint/context-map.ts HOST_BUNDLE_ROOT is src/hosts, and hostBundleImportRestrictions limits what a host imports

whys.why: Why do the contexts stay one implementation for every harness?
whys.because: The rebuild ships one hand-authored core to 7 harnesses, and per-harness branches in the core were the coupling the rebuild removes.
whys.evidence: AGENTS.md section AI-DLC: one core, many harnesses

whyChain.rootCause: The rebuild keeps every harness difference in src/hosts, so the lint layer must know the real harness set, and the folders on disk are its only source.
whyChain.rootCheck: Listed harness/ on 2026-11-08: 7 folders (claude, codex, copilot, cursor, kiro, kiro-ide, opencode); src/hosts does not exist yet, and the reader returns no names for a missing folder.
whyChain.readback: The rebuild keeps harness differences in host bundles, therefore production code outside src/hosts names no harness, therefore the rules need the full harness set, therefore a written copy would drift, therefore lint/harness-folders.ts reads the harness folders through node:fs and node:url.

exceptions.reason: An ESLint rule's listener keys are ESTree node names that ESLint's API fixes.

whys.why: Why does lint/no-comments.ts name a visitor key Program in PascalCase?
whys.because: ESLint calls a rule's listeners by AST node type, and the node type for a whole file is spelled Program.
whys.evidence: https://eslint.org/docs/latest/extend/custom-rules#rule-structure

whys.why: Why does ESLint call listeners by AST node type?
whys.because: ESLint walks the ESTree syntax tree and dispatches each node to the listener whose key matches its type field, so the key equals the ESTree name exactly.
whys.evidence: https://github.com/estree/estree/blob/master/es5.md#programs

whys.why: Why must the listener key equal the ESTree name exactly?
whys.because: Dispatch is a string lookup with no mapping layer, so a camelCase key would never match and the rule would quietly report nothing.
whys.evidence: lint/no-comments.test.ts shows the Program listener reporting a comment on line 1

whys.why: Why would an unmatched camelCase key quietly report nothing?
whys.because: ESLint accepts any extra key on the listener object without validation, so an unmatched name is ignored rather than refused.
whys.evidence: https://eslint.org/docs/latest/extend/selectors

whys.why: Why does ESLint accept an unmatched listener key without validation?
whys.because: Listener keys are CSS-like selectors as well as node names, so ESLint cannot know which strings are mistakes and leaves them to the rule author.
whys.evidence: lint/restrictions.ts writes selectors such as TSAsExpression for no-restricted-syntax

whyChain.rootCause: ESLint's listener keys are selectors and node names its API fixes, so the vendor-facing rule file spells them as ESTree does.
whyChain.rootCheck: Ran bun test lint/no-comments.test.ts on 2026-11-08: the Program listener reported the comment on line 1, and the test passed.
whyChain.readback: ESLint's listener keys are vendor selectors and node names, therefore a rule cannot rename them, therefore the listener for a whole file is spelled Program, therefore lint/no-comments.ts names a visitor key Program in PascalCase.

exceptions.reason: The one place a validated value becomes its branded type; every constructor validates first and then calls it.

whys.why: Why does src/kernel/brand.ts cast its input to the branded type?
whys.because: A branded type carries a phantom marker that no runtime value has, so the compiler can only produce one through a type assertion.
whys.evidence: src/kernel/brand.ts declares brandName as a unique symbol with no runtime value

whys.why: Why do identity values carry a phantom marker the runtime never has?
whys.because: The contracts brand identity values such as ProjectPath and ContentHash so a validated value cannot be swapped for a raw string at compile time.
whys.evidence: src/kernel/values.ts constructors return ProjectPath, SourcePath and ContentHash

whys.why: Why must a validated identity value be kept apart from a raw string at compile time?
whys.because: Each constructor checks portability or format once, and the type is the only proof downstream code holds that the check ran.
whys.evidence: src/kernel/values.ts projectPath validates the segments before it brands

whys.why: Why is the type the only proof downstream code holds that the check ran?
whys.because: Domain modules carry no parsing of their own; they trust values that were validated where they entered.
whys.evidence: git grep on 2026-11-08 finds no zod import under src/workflow-definition/domain or src/kernel/values.ts

whys.why: Why do domain modules carry no parsing of their own?
whys.because: The clean architecture keeps domain and application pure and puts parsing in adapters and constructors, so each value is validated in exactly one constructor.
whys.evidence: lint/restrictions.ts purityRestriction forbids package imports in domain and application

whyChain.rootCause: The clean architecture validates each value in exactly one constructor, so the assertion that brands it exists once, in the kernel helper every constructor calls.
whyChain.rootCheck: Ran the discipline-core audit on 2026-11-08: its only CD-2 finding in src is src/kernel/brand.ts line 11.
whyChain.readback: The clean architecture validates each value in exactly one constructor, therefore the branded type is the downstream proof, therefore identity values carry a phantom marker, therefore src/kernel/brand.ts casts its input to the branded type.

whyChain.rootCause: The rebuild keeps domain and application pure and registers each real IO reach as one named adapter, so Projection's reads of the captured host sources live in host-source-files.ts alone.
